Four subjects, 47 questions, 159 answer items. Every answer was transcribed literally by two models from different vendors, a third arbitrated where they disagreed, and a separate marker applied the school's own answer key and rubrics to the transcript. The teacher's pen marks were read from the pages and are shown beside the machine marks; they were never used to decide a mark.

How a mark is decided

  1. Each scanned page goes to one transcriber, Gemini 3.8 Flash, with the printed questions but never the answer key. They return the student's response for every answer item, literally, plus the teacher's pen marks as a separate field.
  2. Questions the marker flags, and any with an illegible reading, get a second independent reading from Gemini 3.1 Pro. Where the two readings disagree the item stays in review; where they agree the flag can be lifted by the marker.
  3. Answers that span two pages are merged, preferring the non-blank reading.
  4. A separate marker, Claude Sonnet 5, receives only the transcript, the school's answer key, and the rubric, and returns a mark per item with a one-line reason. It never sees the image, so it cannot re-read the handwriting.
  5. Anything that needs a human is flagged: illegible or disputed readings, rubric judgement calls (paragraphs, translations, paraphrase), and any question where the machine mark differs from the teacher's.
Transcriptions are literal; spelling is never corrected. Model readings are shown so a teacher can see where the machines disagreed. Teacher scores are read from the scan and may be misread; they are for comparison only.
